decisions.title: P10 / P11 Security Sequencing
decisions.decision: P10 backend development may proceed later as a project-local, non-network-exposed application/service boundary. P10 MUST NOT expose a production/public/network-facing API or backend surface until the required authentication, CSRF protection, rate limiting, and other applicable security controls have been implemented and authorized through the appropriate security phase. P10 requirements and architecture MUST explicitly preserve this boundary. No assumption is authorized that P10 may expose an insecure public backend merely because P10 is independently listed from P11 in the roadmap. If the exact boundary between 'local/non-network-exposed' and 'network-exposed' needs machine enforcement, that requirement must be made explicit during P10 requirements/architecture. The security controls themselves are NOT implemented now.
scope: Establishes a binding sequencing constraint on P10 backend work
Requires P10 requirements and architecture to preserve the boundary in writing
Defers all authentication, CSRF, rate limiting and related control implementation to the security phase
strict_constraints: No production, public or network-facing API or backend surface from P10 before security controls are implemented AND authorized through the appropriate security phase
No implementation of security controls under this decision
No assumption that independent listing of P10 from P11 implies any network exposure is permitted

decisions.title: P8 / P10 Presentation Ownership
decisions.decision: P8 owns CMS/domain content semantics; the Content / Section / ContentType models; content persistence; authorization semantics; publishing workflow; asset semantics; and the CMS output-safety boundary. P8 remains headless and does not own the actual frontend rendering/presentation implementation. P10 owns domain/frontend/, actual presentation/rendering, frontend composition, rendered HTML output, the serving/presentation surface, domain/backend/ within the security boundary defined by D-P10-1, and domain/shared/ for shared vertical-slice contracts. P10 also owns the interpretation and registry of Section.layout values. P8 may continue storing Section.layout as CMS data, but P8 does not define the presentation meaning of those values. CMS ownership must not be duplicated inside P10.

decisions.title: Frontend Technology Selection
decisions.decision: TECH-FE-STRING-COMPOSITION is SELECTED as the P10 rendering technology. P10 will use project-local plain string composition to generate static/server-rendered HTML, with mandatory per-sink output encoding. The implementation must reuse the already-approved security boundaries established by P8 and P9, including P8's html.escape(text, quote=True), P9's _safe_attr(), and P9's escape_json_ld_for_html(). The renderer must produce the build-directory shape consumed by the P9 audit: **/*.html, robots.txt and sitemap.xml. The technology selection does NOT authorize implementation.

selected_technology.readiness: SUFFICIENT — computed by sps2/core/technology_readiness.py, not read from a stored label
selected_technology.basis_of_selection: This candidate was the only one of the four researched to compute SUFFICIENT: all ten coverage areas COVERED and strongest source rank 1 (official documentation), with direct repository observation of the already-approved P8 and P9 output-safety implementations. The three alternatives remain unselected: TECH-FE-STRING-TEMPLATE and TECH-FE-ELEMENTTREE-HTML compute PARTIAL, and TECH-FE-3RD-PARTY-TEMPLATE-ENGINE computes INSUFFICIENT on the STACK-CONSTRAINT and NOT-RESEARCHED blocking conflicts.

The renderer's output contract is the P9 audit input: a build directory of **/*.html plus robots.txt and sitemap.xml

15. This decision does not authorize P10 implementation.
